questions.stem: A scientist analyses a sample of DNA and finds that 30% of the bases are adenine (A). What percentage of the bases are cytosine (C)?
questions.explanation: Due to complementary base pairing, adenine (A) always pairs with thymine (T), and cytosine (C) always pairs with guanine (G). If 30% of bases are A, then 30% must be T. This accounts for 60% of all bases. The remaining 40% is split equally between C and G, so C = 20% and G = 20%.

questions.stem: DNA is described as a double helix with two antiparallel strands held together by hydrogen bonds. If one strand has the base sequence ATCGGA, what is the complementary sequence on the other strand?
questions.explanation: Using complementary base pairing rules: A pairs with T, T pairs with A, C pairs with G, G pairs with C. So ATCGGA pairs with TAGCCT. Option C contains uracil (U), which is found in RNA, not DNA. The two strands run antiparallel but the base pairing follows the same rules.

questions.stem: A nucleotide is the monomer of DNA. Which three components make up a single DNA nucleotide?

options.text: A phosphate group, a ribose sugar, and a base
A phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and a base
An amino acid, a sugar, and a phosphate group
A phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and an amino acid

questions.explanation: Each DNA nucleotide consists of three parts: a phosphate group, a deoxyribose sugar, and one of four nitrogenous bases (A, T, C, or G). Option A is incorrect because ribose sugar is found in RNA, not DNA. The sugar-phosphate groups form the backbone of each strand, while the bases project inward and pair with those on the opposite strand.

questions.stem: The double helix structure of DNA was discovered by Watson and Crick in 1953, building on X-ray diffraction data from Rosalind Franklin. Why was the X-ray diffraction evidence crucial to their model?

options.text: It showed that DNA was made of amino acids arranged in a chain
It revealed the helical shape and key dimensions of the DNA molecule, which Watson and Crick used to build their structural model
It proved that DNA contained four bases
It showed that DNA replication was semi-conservative

questions.explanation: Franklin's X-ray diffraction photographs (particularly Photo 51) revealed that DNA had a helical structure and provided measurements of the helix diameter and the spacing between turns. Watson and Crick used this physical data, together with Chargaff's base pairing rules, to construct their famous double helix model.

questions.stem: Hydrogen bonds hold the two DNA strands together, while covalent bonds link the nucleotides within each strand. Why is it important that the bonds between the strands are relatively weak hydrogen bonds?

options.text: Weak bonds make the DNA molecule flexible enough to fit inside the cell
Weak hydrogen bonds allow the two strands to separate easily during DNA replication and protein synthesis
Hydrogen bonds make DNA water-soluble so it can dissolve in the cytoplasm
Weak bonds prevent mutations from occurring during cell division

questions.explanation: The hydrogen bonds between complementary bases are individually weak, which is essential because the two strands must separate (unzip) during DNA replication and transcription. If the bonds were too strong, the strands could not be pulled apart by enzymes. The many hydrogen bonds along the entire length still provide enough collective strength to keep the double helix stable under normal conditions.
